Domestic Chinese copper prices have rebounded sharply over the last fortnight with the SHFE 3-month price trading at its highest level since May 2nd . Spot prices as reported by SHMET rose every single day between August 31st and September 9th . On September 13th , the spot market was trading at RMB58,650/t ($9,264/t), well above the LME 3-month price of $8,185/t on the same day. In response to yesterday’s news that the US Federal Reserve is to go ahead with QE3, markets rallied in Asia, driving SHFE copper prices to almost RMB60,000/t, while LME 3-month copper prices have hit 4 ½ month highs this morning. © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **August 2012** www.crugroup.com ## **SHFE inventEstimated cathod stocks on exChinese imports of of imported coppery heads higher (000t)hange and in bonded warehouses ('000 t)concentrate (monthly)** 900

Despite the rally in cathode prices, import premiums remain rather weak, indicating that demand has not yet rebounded. Spot cathode import premiums have been quoted in a range of $50/t to $70/t, a slightly wider range than in our last China Copper Fortnightly, but the average of $60/t remains intact. The premium for SXEW cathode has fallen to $40/t, down from the $50/t we reported two weeks ago. Our survey of market participants indicates that premiums remain depressed because stock levels remain high, and incoming imports are simply adding to an already oversupplied domestic market. Our Beijing office estimates that total bonded warehouse stocks current amount to 675,000 tonnes, an increase of 45,000 tonnes compared to our last reported figure. # Policymakers act to reduce uncertainty Markets had been anticipating additional action by the US Federal Reserve after Chairman Bernanke’s speech of August 31st , in which he refrained from ruling out further stimulus measures. On September 13th , the Fed did announce additional easing measures (the antic

ipated “QE3”) which included increasing the maturing of its purchases of long-term Treasuries, an open-ended buying program of an additional $40 billion per month of mortgage-backed securities, and the guidance that benchmark interest rates would remain at current levels until mid-2013.  On September 7<sup>th</sup> , the ECB effectively created a sovereign debt bailout fund through its intent to buy government bonds.  Taken together, the Fed and ECB actions boosted confidence in the euro, and now make it much more likely for the US dollar to depreciate further against major currencies. 

Turning to China, the first evidence that the central government was likely to look for ways to more actively promote the country’s economic growth, outside of lowering interest rates and easing bank lending, came to light during Premier Wen Jiabao’s inspection tour in Guangdong province on August 24<sup>th</sup> and 25<sup>th</sup> .  His comments at this time focused on helping the export sector to rebound from the slump in Europe.  Indeed, on September 12<sup>th</sup> , the State Council approved measures to speed up the process for paying export tax rebates, expanding trade financing and boosting export-related insurance. 

On September 2<sup>nd</sup> , the website of the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) announced that it would commit to funding RMB 1 trillion (US$157B) in infrastructure projects which have already been proposed by regional governments.  There are 25 railway projects, located in 18 different cities and which will cost roughly RMB800B (US$126.2B).  There are 13 road projects which will cover about 2000km in mostly central and western China.  In addition, 7 port projects have also been approved.  While all of these projects were already included in the current Five-Year Plan, this announcement increases confidence these projects will be implemented.

Speaking at the Davos Summer Forum in Tianjin on September 11<sup>th</sup> , Premier Wen stated that the country was on track to meet its GDP growth target of 7.5% in 2012 and that, if needed, the government could utilize a RMB100B fiscal stability fund to ensure that his occurred. He also noted that the initiatives undertaken by the government so far this year were budgeted and that the government was running a fiscal surplus of about RMB1 trillion year-to-date. 

# More energy efficient products to be subsidized 

Earlier this year in May, the Chinese government announced a new RMB36.3B (US$5.7B) subsidy for energy efficient products including air conditioners, flat-screen TVs, refrigerators, washing machines, water heaters ,energy efficient lights and LEDs, cars, and other highly efficient types of motors (detailed in our May 25<sup>th</sup> CCF).  The government is keen to drive higher rates of energy efficiency in all sectors, however, and it has now turned its attention to fans

, water pumps, condensers, and transformers for industrial use with low efficiency, which together account for around 40% of China’s total power usage. 

The Ministry of Finance (MOF) announced on 9<sup>th</sup> September that it is planning to give a total subsidy of RMB14B (US$2.2B) for six different types of energy efficient products.  This includes desktop computers and air conditioners for consumers along with fans, water pumps, condensers, and transformers for industrial use. The subsidy is expected to result in an additional RMB155.6B (US$24.5B) in consumer and investment spending, and save 31.3 billion kilowatt-hours of power.
